alignments.note: Privative מִן recast as a negative clause takes the complementizer and the negation (rule 48), discontinuous around the clause (rule 25).
Infinitive rendered as a finite verb.
The supplied *the* joins the noun of the expression rather than the adjective it stands before (rule 15).
Second privative מִן takes the complementizer and the negation, with the presentative frame English writes around them; no negative morpheme stands in the clause to claim the *none* (rules 48, 50).
The noun of ensnaring is recast as an English infinitive; head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: Both privative מִן units are headed on their complementizer for parity; *there be none* was kept with the second rather than left added, since the negation is the preposition's own contribution.
